exceptions.reason: R1 chat identity is disabled by default. New tenant-scoped chat tables and alias-only backfill create no owners, bindings or deliveries; no existing table, column, row or route is removed. The permission registry replacement preserves every previous permission and adds only chat.read/send/bind/receive. Legacy inbox writes leave the new nullable chat_thread_id NULL, so existing bodies, same-mode replies, projections, receipts, wakes and harness deliveries retain their legacy path; non-chat events pass the new policy. Native registration triggers retain unowned harness changes and 64-byte observation references, but intentionally reject cross-owner/project/role reuse after an explicit chat claim, mixed reference encodings and alias components beyond 1024; tenant-fence contention can also fail closed. CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION and the alias seed SELECT are conservatively outside the classifier allowlist; this is not a blanket expand-safe or old-binary write-compatibility claim. Evidence: check-migrations.test.mjs verifies the registry superset and exact-byte rejection; internal/chat legacy snapshots, transport/RLS and native-store regressions exercise legacy exclusion and ownership boundaries. CI migration-compat boots the immutable previous binary on the candidate schema and probes health, ready, SPA and authenticated reads, not every legacy write. This exact-byte exception requires coordinator review before merge/release; it does not grant acceptance, enable rollout or skip previous-binary compatibility probes.
